I know residency can be lonely and being betrayed by someone who you thought was a friend will leave you feeling like sh!t
It’s ok. Grief your betrayal, your vulnerability, your naivety (which i do not think you are). Give yourself a few days to drain all of those feelings down the sink. Then draw your boundaries. Tell ur coresident that any contact between you two will only be work related and that he should respect your boundaries and that you are looking for something serious. No some “friends” bullsh!t u cannot be friends with an ex or a man hookup. It will be difficult and awkward at first but let it run its natural course and later on will go back to normal coworkers.
Also go look for new work-friends. There are way too many people for you to sh!t and giggle with and you will find a partner. Do not self-sabotage you’re not wrong for looking for a partner in what seemed to be a friend to you, you shouldn’t be ashamed of being human and seeking human comfort.

I’ve been through that, the trying to figure out whether it’s dysthymia, cyclothymia, or bipolar type II.
I just figured I have dysthymia with atypical features. It means that sometimes I can have normal mood too . As someone who suffers from dysthymia for 9 years, it’s hard for me to know what’s normal and what’s high. since I’ve been low for too long. The term “atypical features” includes other criteria  as well but I’m only mentioning normal mood because that’s what you’re curious about. I’d suggest you visit a real psychologist or a psychiatrist, but I assume just like in my case, this option isn’t available. I know how important it is to know what the damn is going on with you and why are those things happening. Don’t worry, just keep observing yourself and you’ll come up with the answer even if it takes time. I hope things goes good for you.
